16. Dr. Hossain although contends that the Arbitrator was empowered with the power of a Court in awarding interest under section 34 CPC but, as the reference was not in Court, he did not develop the argument on the application of section 34 CPC and mainly relied upon the doctrine of implied power. He referred to a large number of cases of Pakistan, India and English jurisdiction including the decisions in the case of Firm Madanlal Roshanlal Mohajan Vs. Hukumchand Mills Ltd., Indore, AIR 1967 (SC) 1030, Union of India Vs. Bungo Steel Furniture Private Ltd., AIR 1967 (SC) 1032, Ashok Construction Co., 1970 (SCD) 530, State of Orissa Vs. Gokula Chandra Kanungo, 1981 (Orissa) 160 and the case of Chandris Vs. lsbrandtsen Moller Co, Inc, (1950) All England Reports 618. Mr. Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, on the other hand, submits that as the Interest Act, 1839 has been repealed in 1974 by Act 8 of 1973 and as the reference was not in Court the Arbitrator had no authority to award interest by applying the provision of section 34 CPC. He contends that the cases reported in 1967 (SC) 1030 and 1032 referred to by Dr. Hossain were held to be bad law by the Supreme Court of India and he referred us to a decision in the case of Executive Engineer Irrigation, Galimala and others Vs. Abnaduta Jena, 1988 (SC) 1520 and the case of Messrs AZ Chowdhury Vs. Messrs S. Maula Buksh Muhammad Bashir PLD 1965 (SC) 505. 

 In making aforesaid observation the learned Judge of the Supreme Court of India again considered the case of Firm Madanlal Roshanlal Mahajan Vs. Hukumchand Ltd AIR 1961 (SC) 908, Satinder Singh Vs. Umrao Singh, AIR 1960 (SC) 307, Nachippa Chettiar Vs. Subramaniam Chettiar, AIR 1955 (SC) 468, Thawardas Pherumal Vs. Union of India, AIR 1955 (SC) 468, Chandris Vs. Isbrandtsen Moller, 1951-IKB240: 1950-2 All England Reports 618, Bhuwanodas Ramgobind Vs. Harsukhdas Balkishendes AIR 1923 (PC) 66 and Hodgkinson Vs. Ferine, Edwards Vs. Great Western Railway (1857) 9 CB (NS) 189 and it appears that the court held that although section 34 CPC does not apply to arbitration proceedings but the Arbitrator had power to award interest on the implied term of reference. Mr. Ishtiaque Ahmed took a serious objection for application of the principle laid down in those cases on the ground that the observation was made in respect of a references in court and tile decisions have been later on disapproved in the case of Executive Engineer reported in AIR 1988 (SC) 1520. He further placed reliance upon the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. M/s. Saith and Skelton Ltd. and others, 1972 (SC) 1507 and urged that section 34 CPC was not attracted to a proceeding before an Arbitrator. The learned Judges noted that the contention of the appellant in that case was in the absence of any usage or contract, express or implied, or of any provision of law. The award of interest on an amount for the period prior to the date of institution of the suit and interest anterior to the date of the suit cannot be allowed. The appellant in that case relied upon the decisions in the case of Bengal Nagpur Railway Co, Ltd. Vs. Ruttanji Ramji, Thawardas Pherumal Vs. Union of India, Mahabir Prasad Rungla Vs. Durga Dana and Union of India Vs. Bungo Steel Furniture which we have already referred. The Court observed at page 1513: 

 20. Thus, it appears that the arbitrator can award interest prior to the date of institution of the suit. Now, we arc to decide as to whether the principle laid down in the Supreme Court in this regard can be accepted on the facts of the present case before us as the reference was not in court. Dr. Hossain to overcome this difficulty cited the decision of the Court of Appeal in the case of Chandris Vs. Isbrandtsen Moller Co. Inc reported in (1950) All England Reports 618 to contend that the Arbitrator does not derive power from terms of the agreement or from the law but from the submission to him which gives him the implied power. He read the judgment of the Court of Appeal which was delivered by Tucker, L J wherein their Lordships reviewed the cases beginning from 1851 in the case of Edwards Vs. Great Western Railway Co. In that case the question arose whether interest can be awarded by the Arbitrator on the amount awarded for demurrage. It was from judgment on a Special Case delivered by Devlin, J.
